title: Variable Box Visualizer
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Clocks and Watches with AI
description: Step through short Python programs one assignment at a time and predict each variable's new value before the line runs.

learningObjectives: Predict the value of each variable after a sequence of assignment statements
Explain that x = y copies the current value, so changing y later does not change x
Apply the shortcut operators +=, -= and %= by rewriting them as x = x + ...

accessibility.notes: Controls are standard HTML form elements; the canvas has a describe() text for screen readers

keyQuestions: After x = y, does changing y change x?
What does seconds %= 60 do when seconds is 60?
Why does a swap need a third variable in most languages?
commonMisconceptions: x = y links the two names forever
Two assignment lines can run at the same time
assessmentOpportunities: Students predict every value in the "Counter with +=" preset correctly, including 60 % 60 = 0.
Students explain why `a = b` followed by `b = a` does not swap two values.
Students rewrite `seconds %= 60` as an ordinary assignment.

controls.label: Preset
controls.description: Chooses one of four short programs

controls.description: Asks for a prediction before each step
